content.value_statement: Voice changes can break echo cancellation, WebRTC flow, or OpenAI Realtime API behavior. This skill guides Quetrex changes using documented architecture constraints and review checks.
actual_capabilities: Explains the Quetrex always-on microphone and browser echo cancellation architecture.
Identifies the voice files and documentation to review before changes.
Checks proposed edits against WebRTC, OpenAI Realtime API, and browser AEC constraints.
Guides safe updates to audio settings, connection states, UI feedback, and error handling.
Warns against microphone toggling, custom echo cancellation, AudioWorklet bypasses, and artificial delays.
limitations: It is specific to the Quetrex voice architecture and may not fit other products.
It provides guidance only and does not run live audio tests.
It relies on referenced project documentation being present in the target repository.
It does not replace browser testing with real microphones and speakers.

use_cases.title: Review a Voice Change
use_cases.description: Check whether a planned UI or audio change affects microphone state, WebRTC flow, or echo cancellation.

use_cases.title: Protect Architecture Decisions
use_cases.description: Keep implementation work aligned with ADR-001 and the documented Quetrex voice architecture.

use_cases.title: Plan Voice Regression Tests
use_cases.description: Create focused test coverage for echo behavior, permissions, disconnections, browsers, and poor network conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Basic Voice Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned Quetrex voice UI change. Confirm whether it affects microphone state, echo cancellation, audio routing, or OpenAI Realtime API behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Voice Error Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me improve microphone permission and connection error messages in Quetrex. Keep the browser audio pipeline and echo cancellation architecture unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Audio Settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess these proposed media constraints for Quetrex voice quality. Explain risks to browser echo cancellation, WebRTC behavior, and OpenAI Realtime API streaming.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Voice Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Quetrex voice refactor plan against ADR-001, VOICE-SYSTEM.md, and abandoned approaches. Identify architecture violations and required browser tests.

output_examples.input: Can I pause the microphone track during assistant playback?
output_examples.output: Do not pause the track. Keep the microphone enabled, keep echo cancellation enabled, and rely on server-side voice activity detection.

output_examples.input: I want to route audio through an AudioWorklet native bridge.
output_examples.output: Reject this plan for Quetrex. It moves audio outside the browser pipeline and can break browser echo cancellation.

output_examples.input: We need better feedback while voice connects.
output: Safe change: add connection, listening, idle, and error indicators.
Avoid changing microphone enablement, audio routing, or echo cancellation settings.
Test the final behavior in Chrome, Safari, Firefox, and Edge.

best_practices: Read ADR-001 and the voice architecture documentation before changing voice code.
Keep the microphone enabled and browser echo cancellation active during conversations.
Test echo behavior on real browsers with speakers after each voice change.
anti_patterns: Toggling the microphone track to prevent echo during assistant playback.
Routing playback outside the browser audio pipeline.
Adding custom echo cancellation or delay-based gating instead of browser AEC.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It guides Quetrex voice interface changes that involve WebRTC, OpenAI Realtime API, and browser echo cancellation.

faq.question: Which files does it focus on?
faq.answer: It points reviewers to src/lib/openai-realtime.ts and the documented voice architecture decisions.

faq.question: Does it execute commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill metadata allows Read only, and the content is documentation guidance.

faq.question: Can it design a new voice architecture?
faq.answer: It can review alternatives, but it is written to preserve the existing Quetrex architecture.

faq.question: Why does it prefer browser echo cancellation?
faq.answer: The documented Quetrex decision relies on browser AEC because it keeps input and playback in the browser audio graph.

faq.question: Does it replace voice testing?
faq.answer: No. It helps plan and review changes, but real browser and audio-device testing remains required.
